column1: # Known-output expectations for the real-binary check (test/real_tools/check_real_tool.py, .github/workflows/real-tools.yml).
# min_plasmid_share: the least share of the input (a plasmid) that the tool must call plasmid. 0 means the floor is not set yet (any share above zero passes; a share of zero fails):
# no real run had been reviewed when this file was written, so a floor would be a guess. After the first scheduled run, read its summary artifact
# and set the floor from the observed value (a little below it), in a reviewed commit. A tool that rewrites contig names or breaks its output
# format fails regardless of the floor.
# min_recovered: the least fraction of the plasmid's own 31-mers that must be in what the tool called plasmid (0 = not set). Share compares sizes only; this says whether the
# plasmid itself came back. Set from the real-tool run of 2026-11-17 (a little below what each tool showed): mob_recon and platon return contigs of the input, so 1.0;
# plasmidSPAdes, on 600,000 pairs of the real reads SRR11905452, recovered only 0.099 of the 7,154 bp plasmid NZ_CP054231.1 while calling 50 kb (share 7.0): a finding about
# the tool on this fixture, recorded as a regression guard, not as a standard of good performance.

column4: observed share 7.01, recovered 0.099 (2026-11-17); real reads of E. coli EcPF14
